text:
maya: thinking aloud — we need a clearer contract for hedging vs fallback ownership at the edge. currently both gateway and upstream try to decide when to hedge, and that causes double attempts + confusing billing.

sam: agree. observed duplicate hedges on ~0.6% of flows during spikes. expensive and noisy. :grimacing:

oliver: proposal: make hedging decisions single-source-of-truth at the ingress proxy. edge emits a hedging-token header and upstreams treat it as advisory only (no new hedges). if ingress hedges, upstreams must accept or return 425-like signal.

li: how do we handle midflight failover where backend is slow but upstream caches or sidecars can complete cheaper? ingress-only hedging may preclude local optimizations.

maya: good point. suggest split responsibilities: ingress decides whether to hedge globally; upstreams can do local micro-hedges within a bounded window if they own the connection and the hedging-token permits it. token could be structured: "hedge-policy=v1;window=100ms;owner=ingress".

nina: love structured token. need to ensure idempotency safety — we can't let sidecars retry non-idempotent requests without a safe-guard. maybe add an idempotency-hint header or require explicit opt-in.

sam: +1. also we should emit metrics per hedge-owner so billing/observability can attribute extra tokens to ingress vs upstream.

eng-bot: deploy-checklist: update ingress proto, bump header size budget, add metric labels (hedge_owner, hedge_decision_ts), update SDK docs.

oliver: another tradeoff: who holds hedge budget/credits? If upstreams can locally hedge, we might double-count budgets. Simpler: ingress maintains global hedge budget per route; upstreams must request permission via a short control RPC before local hedging (cheap to implement with 1 RPC/100s).

li: that control RPC adds latency though. maybe make it asynchronous: upstream signals intent, ingress returns a lease token that is valid for N ms. if not returned, upstream falls back to conservative behavior.

maya: implementation note: prefer stateless tokens where possible to avoid central coordination hotspot. token contains route, budget-quota, expiry, HMAC. ingress validates and upstreams honor.

sam: perf question: validating HMAC per-request could cost CPU on busy services. maybe only do it for local hedges (rare) and cache validation for 10s.

nina: we also need clear abort semantics — if client cancels after ingress hedge but upstream already started local hedge, which side aborts which connection? define that ingress cancellation is authoritative; upstreams must surface partial responses and cleanly cancel secondary streams.

oliver: agreed. add explicit header: "x-rw-hedge-session: <id>" so aborts can correlate across hops.

maya: actionable: I'll sketch a small RFC with examples + header grammar + sample tokens. owners: maya (draft), sam (perf validation), oliver (upstream guidance), li (safety/idempotency rules), nina (telemetry). aim for RFC by EOD Friday.

sam: will run a short load test to reproduce the double-hedge and measure CPU hit if we HMAC-validate.

li: I'll write idempotency hint proposal and default safe behavior for non-hinted requests.

nina: will add telemetry labels and dashboard mockups.

maya: thanks all. quick thing — here's a config sketch we can use in the RFC:

```yaml
edge.hedging:
  enabled: true
  global_budget_per_route: 0.05 # fraction of requests
  token_expiry_ms: 150
  default_window_ms: 75
  idempotency_required_for_local_hedge: true
```

sam: looks good. also include cost-estimate section comparing current double-hedge vs single-owner hedge.

eng-bot: NOTE: remember to run security review for HMAC secrets if we sign tokens. :lock:

maya: noted. I'll include key rotation plan.

oliver: tiny UX: add a debug header so devs can see hedge decisions end-to-end: "x-rw-hedge-debug: ingress=skipped,upstream=allowed". helps troubleshoot.

maya: perfect. RFC will include examples, sequence diagrams, and a staged rollout plan (opt-in route flag -> global default).

sam: thanks — ping when RFC draft exists, will test in canary staging.

maya: will do. end thread.
